title: Rate of reaction; Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms: 4.6.1-c17, 4.6.1-c11, 4.6.1-c21, 4.6.1-c16. Clues: 4.6.1-c17 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c11 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c21 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.6.1-c16 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.6.1-q14, 4.6.1-q18, 4.6.1-q25, 4.6.2-q01, 4.6.2-q05, 4.6.2-q07, 4.6.1-q15, 4.6.1-q19, 4.6.1-q26, 4.6.2-q02, 4.6.2-q06, 4.6.2-q08, 4.6.2-q09, 4.6.2-q13, 4.6.2-q17, 4.6.2-q22, 4.6.2-q10, 4.6.2-q14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Frequency of collisions
items.clue: How many collisions happen each second.

items.label: Concentration
items.clue: The amount of a dissolved substance in a given volume of solution.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: A substance that changes the rate of a chemical reaction but is not used up during the reaction.

items.label: Collision theory
items.clue: Chemical reactions can occur only when reacting particles collide with each other and with sufficient energy.

questions.stem: Which list contains only factors that the specification says affect the rate of a chemical reaction?

options.text: Concentration, pressure of gases, surface area, temperature, time
Concentration, pressure of gases, surface area, temperature, catalysts
Concentration, colour of the reactants, temperature, stirring, catalysts
Concentration, pressure of gases, surface area, pH, volume of flask

questions.explanation: This is exactly the list the specification gives.

questions.stem: According to collision theory, when can a reaction between two particles take place?

options.text: Whenever they collide, no matter how gently they hit each other
Only when the collision itself gives out enough energy
Only when they collide with at least the activation energy
Whenever they are in the same container as each other

questions.explanation: Reactions can occur only when reacting particles collide with each other and with sufficient energy.

questions.stem: Which statement about catalysts is correct?

options.text: A catalyst is used up slowly, so more must be added as it goes
One catalyst will speed up any reaction that it is added to
A catalyst changes the rate of a reaction but is not used up by it
A catalyst makes a reaction produce more of the product

questions.explanation: Catalysts change the rate of chemical reactions but are not used up during the reaction.

questions.stem: Which statement describes what makes a reaction a reversible reaction?

options.text: The products of the reaction can react to produce the original reactants
The reaction goes fully forwards and then it goes fully backwards
The reaction finishes with equal amounts of reactants and products
The reaction can be made faster or slower by a change of conditions

questions.explanation: This is the definition given in the specification: in some chemical reactions the products can react to produce the original reactants.

questions.stem: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is exothermic. What can be said about the reverse reaction?

options.text: It is exothermic as well and transfers the same amount of energy back
It is endothermic and transfers the same amount of energy as the forward one
It is endothermic but it transfers less energy than the forward one
It is endothermic and the energy transferred depends on the rate

questions.explanation: If a reversible reaction is exothermic in one direction it is endothermic in the opposite direction, and the same amount of energy is transferred.

questions.stem: A reversible reaction takes place in a sealed flask. When is the mixture at equilibrium?

options.text: When both the forward and the reverse reactions have completely stopped
When the amounts of all the reactants and of all the products are the same
When all of the reactants have been converted into the products
When the forward and reverse reactions occur at exactly the same rate

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition of equilibrium in apparatus which prevents the escape of reactants and products.

questions.stem: A reaction mixture is cooled from 40 °C to 20 °C. What happens to the rate of the reaction?

options.text: It increases, because cooling packs the particles closer together
It decreases, as collisions are less frequent and less energetic
It is unchanged, since temperature affects only the final amount made
It decreases, but only if a catalyst is taken out as well

questions.explanation: Students should be able to recall that lowering the temperature lowers the rate.

questions.stem: What is meant by the activation energy of a reaction?

options.text: The energy given out as the products are formed
The energy that is given out when the particles collide and react
The minimum energy that particles must have in order to react
The total energy needed to make all the particles react

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition of activation energy.

questions.stem: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a chemical reaction?

options.text: It provides a different pathway with a lower activation energy
It lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway
It speeds up any reaction at all, as catalysts always do
It makes the reaction produce more product, so it goes faster

questions.explanation: This is the specification's explanation of catalytic action.

questions.stem: A reversible reaction is represented as A + B ⇌ C + D. What does the ⇌ symbol tell you?

options.text: That the mixture holds equal amounts of A, B, C and D throughout it
That the reaction can go in the forward and the reverse direction
That the mixture has already reached equilibrium at every moment
That the forward reaction is faster than the reverse reaction

questions.explanation: The double arrow is the way the specification represents a reversible reaction: A and B can form C and D, and C and D can form A and B.

questions.stem: Heating blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate to form white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate and water takes in 45 kJ of energy. Water is then added to the white solid. What happens to the energy?

options.text: Less than 45 kJ is given out, because some energy is lost as heat
45 kJ is taken in, because this change also needs energy
45 kJ is given out, as the same amount of energy is transferred
Most of the 45 kJ is given out, but some is always lost

questions.explanation: The reverse reaction is exothermic and, as the specification states, the same amount of energy is transferred in each case.

questions.stem: Why must a reversible reaction be carried out in apparatus that prevents reactants and products escaping if equilibrium is to be reached?

options.text: Escaped products cannot take part in reverse reactions
The reverse reaction happens anyway, whatever escapes
Equilibrium means nothing at all is allowed to move about
The reactants and products must be present in equal amounts

questions.explanation: The reverse rate can only rise to match the forward rate if the products stay in the mixture, so escape prevents equilibrium.

questions.stem: The same reversible reaction is allowed to reach equilibrium at two different temperatures. What can be said about the amounts of the substances present?

options.text: The amounts must be equal at equilibrium whatever conditions are used
The amounts depend only on how quickly equilibrium was reached
The relative amounts of the reactants and products depend on the conditions
The amounts are fixed by the masses that were mixed at the start

questions.explanation: The specification states that the relative amounts of all the reactants and products at equilibrium depend on the conditions of the reaction.

questions.stem: The concentration of one substance in a mixture at equilibrium is changed. What happens to the concentrations of the other substances?

options.text: Only the substance whose concentration was altered is different
They stay the same, as the system is always at equilibrium
They change only when the temperature is altered as well
They all change until equilibrium is reached again in the mixture

questions.explanation: The system is no longer at equilibrium, and the concentrations of all the substances change until equilibrium is reached again.

questions.stem: The forward reaction of a reversible reaction is endothermic. The temperature of the system at equilibrium is increased. What happens to the relative amount of products?

options.text: It increases, because the reaction is endothermic in the forward direction
It decreases, because raising the temperature will release more energy
It decreases, because the reactants are used up much more quickly
It stays the same, because heating changes only the reaction rates

questions.explanation: The relative amount of products at equilibrium increases for an endothermic reaction when the temperature is increased.

questions.stem: For the gaseous equilibrium N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g), the pressure is increased. Which way does the equilibrium position shift?

options.text: Towards nitrogen and hydrogen, the side with more molecules
Neither way, as pressure cannot alter this mixture
Towards the ammonia, the side with the fewer molecules
Towards the nitrogen, which has heavier molecules

questions.explanation: An increase in pressure shifts the position towards the side with the smaller number of molecules: four on the left, two on the right.

questions.stem: A system at equilibrium has one of its conditions changed. According to the specification, how does the system respond?

options.text: It responds until the change made to it has been cancelled out completely
It stays exactly as it was, because it is already at equilibrium
It stops reacting until the original conditions are restored
It responds in the direction that counteracts the change that was made

questions.explanation: If a system at equilibrium has a condition changed, the system responds to counteract the change.

questions.stem: For the equilibrium CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O, more ethanol (C2H5OH) is added. What happens?

options.text: More products form until equilibrium is reached again in the flask
More reactants form, because ethanol was added to the reactant side
Nothing changes at all, since the total mass has not altered
The reaction speeds up but no extra ester is being formed

questions.explanation: If the concentration of a reactant is increased, more products will be formed until equilibrium is reached again.
